title: 2017 HMMT November Theme Problem 7
statement: On a blackboard a stranger writes the values of \(s_{7}(n)^{2}\) for \(n=0,1, \ldots, 7^{20}-1\), where \(s_{7}(n)\) denotes the sum of digits of \(n\) in base 7. Compute the average value of all the numbers on the board.

solutions.text:
We solve for 0 to \(b^{n}-1\) and \(s_{b}(n)^{2}\) (i.e. base \(b\) ).
Let \(n=d_{1} \ldots d_{n}\) in base \(b\), where there may be leading zeros. Then \(s_{b}(n)=d_{1}+\cdots+d_{n}\), regardless of the leading zeros.

\[\mathbb{E}\left[s_{d}(n)^{2}\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[\left(d_{1}+\cdots+d_{n}\right)^{2}\right]=\sum_{1 \leq i \leq n} \mathbb{E}\left[d_{i}^{2}\right]+2 \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq n} \mathbb{E}\left[d_{i} d_{j}\right]\]

and now notice that we can treat choosing \(n\) uniformly as choosing the \(d_{i}\) uniformly independently from \(\{0, \ldots, b-1\}\). Thus this simplifies to

\[\mathbb{E}\left[s_{d}(n)^{2}\right]=n \mathbb{E}\left[d_{1}^{2}\right]+n(n-1) \mathbb{E}\left[d_{1}\right]^{2}\]

Now

\[\begin{gathered}
\mathbb{E}\left[d_{1}^{2}\right]=\frac{0^{2}+\cdots+(b-1)^{2}}{b}=\frac{(b-1)(2 b-1)}{6} \\
\mathbb{E}\left[d_{1}\right]=\frac{0+\cdots+(b-1)}{b}=\frac{b-1}{2}
\end{gathered}\]

so the answer is

\[n \cdot \frac{(b-1)(2 b-1)}{6}+n(n-1) \cdot\left(\frac{b-1}{2}\right)^{2}\]

Plugging in \(b=7, n=20\) yields the result.
